report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of vendors.py: VendorReply, FloorRefusal, RunResult dataclasses; floor_check and _withheld_paths functions; validated docstring claims against code.
risks: floor_check | medium | Docstring says secret_floor_rule returns rule on hit, but code uses rule.startswith("secret path marker") to assign channel. If rule format changes, channel assignment may be wrong. | Check secret_floor_rule return format.

_withheld_paths | low | Function name suggests it returns paths withheld, but code returns paths that slice_egress_rule returns truthy for. If slice_egress_rule returns truthy for allowed paths, logic is inverted. | Verify slice_egress_rule semantics.
todos: Verify secret_floor_rule return value format to confirm channel assignment logic.
Confirm slice_egress_rule return semantics for allow-list vs block-list.

handoff.purpose: Define VendorReply, FloorRefusal, RunResult dataclasses and implement floor_check and _withheld_paths functions for secret floor enforcement and tier-2 allow-listing.

symbols.name: VendorReply
symbols.note: Dataclass with fields: vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld. Has __post_init__ validating status and lane.

symbols.name: RunResult
symbols.note: Dataclass with fields: returncode (int|None), stdout (str), stderr (str), timed_out (bool), spawn_error (str).

symbols.name: floor_check
symbols.note: Runs secret floor on evidence paths, evidence files, and prompt. Returns FloorRefusal or None. Uses secret_floor_rule and assigns channel based on rule prefix.

symbols.name: _withheld_paths
symbols.note: Returns tuple of paths withheld by tier-2 allow-list for untrusted lanes. Uses slice_egress_rule.

claims.text: A council prompt is question + evidence + a multi-file diff, so there is no single ``path``
claims.why: This claim describes the structure of a council prompt, which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: the tempting ``secret_floor_rule("", prompt)`` kills the path tier outright: a patch that ADDS ``.env`` or ``config/id_rsa`` sails through, because the only trace of the filename is ``diff --git a/.env b/.env`` inside ``text``, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: This describes a behavior of secret_floor_rule that is not testable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: evidence_paths -- every changed path (PatchArtifact.changed_paths) and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone
claims.why: References PatchArtifact.changed_paths which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: evidence_files -- (path, text) pairs, both channels, per file
claims.why: The code iterates over evidence_files and calls secret_floor_rule(path, text or '') which checks both path and content.

claims.text: prompt -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself. It is a backstop, never the whole check.
claims.why: The code calls secret_floor_rule('', prompt or '') after checking evidence_paths and evidence_files, so it serves as a backstop.

claims.text: Returns the first FloorRefusal, or None. A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: The code returns a FloorRefusal on first rule match, otherwise returns None.

claims.text: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list, and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: References OpenAI/Google and reply naming which are not in this chunk.

observations.what: VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status against STATUSES and lane against LANES, but these constants are not defined in this chunk.

floor_check docstring claims that secret_floor_rule returns a rule string on hit, and the code uses rule.startswith('secret path marker') to determine channel. This ties channel logic to the rule string prefix.

_withheld_paths returns paths where slice_egress_rule returns truthy. The docstring says 'allow-list', implying truthy means withheld, but the function name says 'withheld paths'. This could be inverted.
